_about: Care pathway definitions. Each entry is one disease the coordinator can run. Add an entry to add a disease: no code changes needed. example_* fields only pre-fill the demo screens.

pathways.name: Suspected pulmonary tuberculosis
pathways.imaging_focus: findings that can be associated with pulmonary TB: upper-lobe infiltrates or consolidation, cavitation, hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy, miliary nodules, pleural effusion, fibrotic scarring
pathways.lab_focus: whether M. tuberculosis was detected or not detected, the bacterial load if reported, and rifampicin resistance status
pathways.follow_up_plan: Weekly adherence and symptom check-in while treatment is active.
escalation_rules: 3 or more missed doses in the past week
coughing up blood
yellow eyes or skin, dark urine (possible liver injury)
persistent vomiting or unable to take medicines
new or worsening breathlessness or chest pain
new vision problems or numbness/tingling
pathways.completion_rule: The doctor's notes say the treatment course is finished.
pathways.example_symptoms: Cough for 3 weeks, evening fever, night sweats, weight loss of about 4 kg
pathways.example_doctor_notes: Start first-line TB treatment as per national guidelines. Daily doses, review in clinic in 2 weeks. Course length 6 months.

example_check_ins.on_track: Took all 7 doses this week. Cough is less. No other problems.
example_check_ins.warning: Missed 4 doses this week because of travel. Feeling nauseous and my eyes look a bit yellow.
example_check_ins.finished: Finished the full course as the doctor said. Feeling well, no cough.

pathways.name: Suspected community-acquired pneumonia
pathways.imaging_focus: findings that can be associated with pneumonia: lobar or segmental consolidation, air bronchograms, patchy infiltrates, pleural effusion; say which lung zone is affected
pathways.lab_focus: the white cell count, neutrophils and CRP, and whether each is above, within or below the reference range printed in the report
pathways.follow_up_plan: Check-in every 2 to 3 days during the antibiotic course, then once at the end.
escalation_rules: breathless at rest or breathing getting worse
confusion, unusual drowsiness or fainting
fever still high after 3 days of treatment
lips or fingertips turning bluish
new or worsening chest pain
unable to keep fluids or medicines down
2 or more missed antibiotic doses
pathways.completion_rule: The patient reports finishing the antibiotic course and feeling better, and the doctor's notes say no further review is needed.
pathways.example_symptoms: Fever and cough with yellow sputum for 4 days, pain on the right side of the chest when breathing in, breathless climbing stairs
pathways.example_doctor_notes: Start oral antibiotics as per clinic protocol for community-acquired pneumonia, 5-day course. Paracetamol for fever. Review in clinic in 3 days, no further review needed after that if recovered.

example_check_ins.on_track: Fever went away yesterday, cough is less, taking the antibiotics on time.
example_check_ins.warning: Still high fever after 3 days of antibiotics and now I get breathless just sitting.
example_check_ins.finished: Finished the 5-day course. No fever, breathing is normal, feeling well.

pathways.name: Suspected dengue fever
pathways.lab_focus: whether dengue NS1 antigen and IgM are positive or negative, the platelet count and haematocrit, and whether each is outside the reference range printed in the report
pathways.follow_up_plan: Daily check-in during the critical phase (about days 3 to 7 of illness), then once at recovery.
escalation_rules: severe abdominal pain or vomiting again and again
bleeding from gums or nose, or blood in vomit or stool
unusual drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
cold, clammy skin or fainting
unable to drink enough fluids, or passing very little urine
pathways.completion_rule: The patient reports no fever for at least 2 days and feeling well, and the doctor's notes say no further review is needed.
pathways.example_symptoms: High fever for 3 days, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, body and joint aches, mild rash
pathways.example_doctor_notes: Supportive care as per clinic protocol: plenty of oral fluids, paracetamol for fever; avoid ibuprofen and aspirin. Repeat platelet count in 2 days. No further review needed after recovery.

example_check_ins.on_track: Fever settled yesterday, drinking plenty of water, eating a little, no bleeding.
example_check_ins.warning: Severe stomach pain since morning, vomiting again and again, and my gums bled while brushing.
example_check_ins.finished: No fever for three days now, appetite is back and I feel well.

pathways.name: Suspected type 2 diabetes
pathways.lab_focus: HbA1c and fasting glucose values, and whether each is in the normal, prediabetes or diabetes range according to the report's reference ranges
pathways.follow_up_plan: Monthly glucose log and medication adherence check-in.
escalation_rules: any glucose reading above 300 mg/dL or below 70 mg/dL
confusion, fainting or extreme thirst
a foot wound that is not healing
3 or more missed doses in the past week
pathways.completion_rule: The doctor's notes say routine follow-up is handed over to the clinic.
pathways.example_symptoms: Increased thirst and frequent urination for 2 months, tiredness, blurred vision
pathways.example_doctor_notes: Start metformin as per clinic protocol. Diet and exercise counselling. Repeat HbA1c in 3 months, then routine follow-up handed over to the clinic.

example_check_ins.on_track: Sugar readings between 110 and 150 this month, taking my tablets daily, no problems.
example_check_ins.warning: Readings went above 320 twice this week and I felt very thirsty and dizzy.
example_check_ins.finished: Three months done, HbA1c repeated, the doctor handed my follow-up to the clinic.

pathways.name: Suspected hypertension (high blood pressure)
pathways.lab_focus: the blood pressure readings, creatinine, urine protein and cholesterol values, and whether each is above or within the reference range printed in the report
pathways.follow_up_plan: Weekly home blood pressure log for the first month, then monthly.
escalation_rules: any blood pressure reading of 180/120 mmHg or higher
severe headache, blurred vision or confusion
chest pain or breathlessness
weakness or numbness on one side, or trouble speaking
3 or more missed doses in the past week
pathways.completion_rule: The doctor's notes say blood pressure is controlled and routine follow-up is handed over to the clinic.
pathways.example_symptoms: Morning headaches for a month, blood pressure 158/98 at a pharmacy check, family history of high blood pressure
pathways.example_doctor_notes: Start blood pressure medicine as per clinic protocol. Reduce salt and walk daily. Weekly home BP log, review in 4 weeks; routine follow-up handed over to the clinic once controlled.

example_check_ins.on_track: Home readings this week were between 128/82 and 136/86. Taking the tablet every morning.
example_check_ins.warning: Reading this morning was 186/122 and I have a bad headache and blurry vision.
example_check_ins.finished: Readings have been under 135/85 for a month and the doctor handed my follow-up to the clinic.
